question.text: Fund TCR (Cat III Long-Short) holds: BUY Company B INR 5 cr, SELL Company C INR 7.5 cr, BUY Company D INR 20 cr, BUY Company E INR 5 cr, SELL Company F INR 9.3 cr. Additionally it bought Put options worth INR 1.125 cr. What is the NET equity exposure (ignoring options)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Longs = 5 + 20 + 5 = INR 30 cr. Shorts = 7.5 + 9.3 = INR 16.8 cr. Net = 30 - 16.8 = INR 13.2 cr LONG. The Trap: Option A sums all longs only. Option C is longs excluding D. Option B is the short total (wrong sign). Cross-Exam Context: PDF Example 10.2 math. XIX-C same. Manager's Pro-Tip: Don't forget the option delta: a deep OTM Put has tiny delta contribution; ATM Puts contribute ~-0.50 of notional. In Example 10.2 the Puts add ~-INR 0.56 cr of effective short delta — trivial vs the 13.2 cr net long. NAV-level delta is what matters for Beta reporting.
